title: AI Agile Pipeline
description: The agent dependency graph that the orchestrator uses to decide which agent runs next. See docs/product/orchestrator/05-pipeline-config.md.

budgets.description: Consumption limits: a default turn/wall-clock budget every agent-type step gets unless it declares its own override, and a pipeline-wide cap on how much work one tick starts. Moves AGENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS and PIPELINE_MAX_CONCURRENT out of pipeline_orchestrator.py and into config (AS-1).

max_turns.description: Default turn budget for every agent-type step, unless the step declares its own via its own budgets.max_turns.

max_wall_seconds.description: Default wall-clock budget for every agent-type step, unless the step declares its own via its own budgets.max_wall_seconds. Script-type steps use script_timeout_seconds instead, unaffected by this field.

max_launches_per_tick.description: How much work a single tick will start before it stops, so a burst of eligible work does not consume everything available in one pass. Pipeline-wide only -- no per-step equivalent.

defaults.description: Pipeline-level defaults merged into every agent invocation.

extra_allowedTools.description: Tools prepended to every agent's extra_allowedTools. Agents can extend this list in their own frontmatter.

agent_lifecycle.description: Scripts the orchestrator runs around every agent invocation, to prepare and tear down the environment the agent runs in. Not pipeline steps: they emit no AI_AGILE_STATUS sentinel, take no label, and a non-zero exit is logged and ignored rather than failing the run. Agent steps only. See docs/product/orchestrator/05-pipeline-config.md.

before.description: Repo-relative script paths run immediately before each invocation, including each retry. Must be idempotent: a run killed mid-flight leaves state behind, and re-running setup is what clears it.

after.description: Repo-relative script paths run once after the final retry, on every outcome (complete, review, blocked, non-zero exit, retries exhausted).

agent.description: Stable agent name in the form {phase}/{short-name}; matches the prompt at .claude/agents/{phase}/{short-name}.md and the name: field in that prompt's frontmatter. The phase prefix is numeric-prefixed (e.g. 01_product_docs) so the directory tree sorts in lifecycle order. 00_ondemand holds human-triggered agents outside the lifecycle flow. The phase prefix must equal the phase field. See docs/product/orchestrator/PRODUCT.md, 'The agent prompt file'.

trigger.description: One or more trigger shapes. The orchestrator fires when ANY shape is satisfied.

branch_suffix.description: Suffix appended to the issue-{N} branch name for this step's commit_after checkout (e.g. '-docs' targets issue-{N}-docs). Empty or absent means the default code branch issue-{N}. Used by the two-phase design-to-build flow (issue #247) so prd-docs-updater commits to the design branch while coder commits to the code branch.

auto_approve_on_complete.description: When true and the agent emits :complete, the orchestrator automatically applies human_gate_label without requiring a human to act. Use for agents whose :review path needs a gate (conflicted PRs) but whose :complete path should advance uninterrupted (clean PRs).

self_gates.description: When true, the orchestrator trusts the agent's own AI_AGILE_STATUS (review vs complete) instead of force-overriding :complete to :review. Use for agents where only some runs warrant human review (e.g. prd-docs-updater: review only when docs/product/ prose changed, complete when the run was mechanical-only). human_gate_after/human_gate_label still apply for promotion once the agent itself emits :review. Mutually exclusive in practice with auto_approve_on_complete, which instead always suppresses the gate on :complete.

session.description: Session management configuration for this agent. Controls whether the claude CLI is invoked with a per-issue session ID or a single shared session ID across all issues.

scope.description: per_issue — unique session per work item; default ID: ais-v1-{safe_agent}-issue-{number}. global — one persistent session for all invocations of this agent; default ID: ais-v1-{safe_agent}. Use global for agents that benefit from accumulated context across issues (e.g. doc reviewers).

id_pattern.description: Optional token pattern for the session ID. Available tokens: {agent}, {safe_agent}, {phase}, {safe_phase}, {number}, {kind}, {owner}, {repo_name}, {safe_repo}. Only bare {identifier} placeholders are allowed — attribute/index access is rejected. When omitted the built-in default for the chosen scope is used. See docs/product/orchestrator/05-pipeline-config.md §Session ID tokens.

type.description: Invocation mode. 'agent' (default) invokes Claude CLI with the matching .claude/agents/{phase}/{name}.md prompt. 'script' runs the file at the 'script' path directly via bash with the standard environment variables.

script.description: Repo-relative path to the shell script to execute. Required when type is 'script'; ignored otherwise.

max_retries.description: How many times the orchestrator will re-invoke this step after a :failed outcome before giving up. 0 means no retries (fail immediately).

model.description: Which model this agent-type step runs on, chosen when the step was declared -- a step does not choose its own model (AS-1). Not a frontmatter field; the prompt file at .claude/agents/{agent}.md declares only name and description.

budgets.description: Overrides the top-level budgets default for this agent-type step only, field by field: a step declaring only max_turns still inherits max_wall_seconds from the default, and vice versa. Absent entirely means this step uses the default for both.

max_turns.description: Bounds how much back-and-forth this step's invocation is allowed.

max_wall_seconds.description: Bounds how long this step's invocation may hold the pipeline. A :wip older than this cannot still be legitimately running and is reclaimed.

expected_effect.description: What this step is supposed to change, declared explicitly so the orchestrator can compare it against what actually changed (MI-6). A step declaring no commits that produces one disagrees with itself.

commits.description: Whether this step is expected to change tracked files.

creates_issues.description: Whether this step is expected to raise a new work item.

allowed_labels.description: Which labels this step may ask the orchestrator to add or remove, as part of its returned result. A step never writes to GitHub itself; it requests, and the orchestrator applies only what this declares, silently dropping the rest. Absent means the step may request no label changes. Patterns follow the same glob convention as extra_allowedTools.

add.description: Label patterns this step may request be added, to its own item or another named in the request.

remove.description: Label patterns this step may request be removed, to its own item or another named in the request.

max_concurrent.description: Maximum concurrent instances of this agent type across all work items in a single orchestrator tick. The orchestrator counts :wip labels before launching and skips eligible work items once this ceiling is reached. Null or absent means 1 (default). A pipeline-wide aggregate ceiling (see PIPELINE_MAX_CONCURRENT in pipeline_orchestrator.py for the authoritative value) applies across all agent types regardless of per-agent values.

git_ops.description: Declares that this agent produces file output the orchestrator should commit, push, and optionally open a PR for. Absent means the agent does not produce file output.

commit_after.description: When true the orchestrator stages all changes and creates a commit after the agent exits successfully.

branch_prefix.description: Prefix for the branch the orchestrator creates before invoking the agent. Final branch name: {branch_prefix}{issue_number}.

pr_lifecycle.description: When true the orchestrator opens a draft PR before invoking the agent (on the branch identified by branch_prefix).

post_steps.description: Ordered list of repo-relative paths to bash scripts the orchestrator runs after the agent signals :complete. Each script runs with REPO, WORK_ITEM_KIND, WORK_ITEM_NUMBER, AGENT_NAME, ISSUE_NUMBER (or PR_NUMBER), and AI_AGILE_ROOT set. A non-zero exit transitions the work item from :complete to :failed.

review_gate.description: Set true only on the agent that acts as the final automated review gate before human merge approval (currently pr-reviewer). Controls whether unresolved human REQUEST_CHANGES reviews trigger a free coder re-invoke. Independent of post_steps.

exclude_classifications.description: Skip this agent when the issue classification matches any value in this list. Classification is read from a 'classification: {type}' label or a '[TYPE]' title prefix applied by issue-classifier.

exclude_labels.description: Skip this agent when any of these labels is present on the work item. Use to prevent pipeline stages running on epics ('epic') or issues blocked by sub-issues ('blocked').

review_loop.description: Automatic retry loop: when this agent emits :review, the orchestrator re-invokes a target agent (up to max_cycles times) before escalating to human sign-off. Only applies to agents that emit :review.

re_invoke.description: The agent to re-invoke when this agent requests changes. Must be an earlier stage in the pipeline (e.g. coder for pr-reviewer).

max_cycles.description: Maximum number of retry cycles. After this many REQUEST CHANGES verdicts, the orchestrator escalates to human sign-off.

also_clear.description: Additional agent names whose :complete label is also cleared when the review loop fires, so intermediate steps re-run on the next cycle (e.g. ci-gate between coder and pr-reviewer).

extra_allowedTools.description: Additional tools allowed for this agent beyond the pipeline defaults. Merged with defaults.extra_allowedTools at invocation time.

script_timeout_seconds.description: Override the default script timeout (seconds) for script-type steps that need longer polling windows (e.g. ci-gate).
